gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the US 120 V DJI Power 1000 (DYM1000L) holds its 2,600 W max output for only 30 seconds, while the 230 V model holds it for 60 seconds. DJI publishes no hold time for the 4,400 W peak that ChatGPT used to rank it.
standout_why: Pages compared: Volt & Valley Best Portable Power Stations 2026 (cited), Volt & Valley high-surge-load guide, Tested Watts C1000 Gen 2 vs DELTA 3 Plus (cited). Volt & Valley's surge guide says no maker in its registry publishes how long a surge rating is held, and neither Volt & Valley page mentions regional versions. Tested Watts gives no surge duration for any unit. None of them says DJI publishes a 30 s / 60 s overload hold that differs by region. None of them notes that BLUETTI's US page lists the Elite 100 V2 at 1,800 W with 2,700 W of 'Lifting Power' and gives no 3,600 W surge figure. ChatGPT's table used that 3,600 W number. I could not open the Tested Watts BLUETTI vs EcoFlow page (cited) because of a TLS certificate error.
decides: It weakens ChatGPT's surge-per-pound ranking. DJI Power 1000 stays a strong pick, and its maker gives the clearest hold-time figure: 2,600 W for 30 s on the 120 V unit, or about 91 W/lb, compared with 153 W/lb from the undated 4,400 W peak. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 drops from ChatGPT's ~142 W/lb to 108 W/lb if you use the only output figure on BLUETTI's US page (2,700 W Lifting Power, 25 lb). The page should rank by the figure each maker actually publishes for US 120 V units and should name the region.

findings.label: Max output and hold time, US 100-120 V model (DYM1000L)
findings.note: Prototype figure at about 25 °C and 50% battery; DJI says it 'may vary'. The 220-240 V DYM1000H holds 2,600 W for 60 s. 2,600 W ÷ 28.66 lb (13 kg) = about 91 W/lb.

findings.label: Continuous and peak AC output
findings.value: 2,200 W continuous; 4,400 W peak (no duration given)
findings.note: Both the L and H models list 2,200 W continuous 'until the battery runs out' at 25 °C. DJI says AC output varies by region; the Japanese 100 V version is limited to 2,000 W. 4,400 W ÷ 28.66 lb = about 153.5 W/lb.

findings.label: Bypass (pass-through) output, US model
findings.note: Applies when the unit runs plugged into the wall. On the US unit, a load above 1,440 W in bypass is outside spec.

findings.label: AC output as listed on BLUETTI US store
findings.value: 1,800 W rated (120 V, 15 A); 2,700 W Lifting Power; no surge figure listed
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 Portable Power Station | BLUETTI US
findings.note: The store listing at /products/elite-100-v2-portable-power-station (read via storecheck) has the same wording: '1,800W output (2,700W Lifting Power)'. Volt & Valley describes BLUETTI Lifting figures as for 'purely resistive loads'. 2,700 W ÷ 25 lb = 108 W/lb, against ChatGPT's 3,600 W ÷ 25.4 lb ≈ 142 W/lb.

findings.value: 1,800 W AC; 2,200 W X-Boost; 3,600 W surge; $579

findings.label: EcoFlow's own X-Boost load claims compared with rival advice
findings.value: EcoFlow US store copy says X-Boost supports 'refrigerators, coffee makers, washers, and circular saws' (DELTA 3 Max) and 'microwaves, refrigerators… and air conditioner' (DELTA 3 Classic)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic Portable Power Station (1024Wh)
findings.note: Volt & Valley's high-surge guide says boost modes are 'the wrong setting for anything with a motor' and to 'never' use them for compressors. The maker's marketing contradicts that, so the page should send shoppers to the manual rather than the marketing. The DELTA 3 Max wording is on https://us.ecoflow.com/products/ecoflow-delta-3-max-plus-portable-power-station.

findings.label: Rival coverage of surge duration
findings.value: Volt & Valley says no maker in its registry publishes how long surge is held
findings.source_title: Best Power Station for High Surge Output and Hard Starts | Volt & Valley
findings.note: DJI's specs page does publish a 30 s / 60 s hold at 2,600 W, so this rival claim does not hold for DJI.
